samples.rationale: A and C edge out the rest by using cream/beige upper wall panels that match the concept's half-timber plaster infill, while B/D/E/F/G all substitute a pink/salmon tone that reads as a material error; all seven builds share the same fundamental gap against the concept — the stepped eave overhang, proper timber-framing relief, window shutters, and door lantern are absent, leaving every candidate a rough massing approximation rather than a realized Tudor craft piece.

F and G use cream/sandstone infill panels that match the concept's plaster tone, while A–E use pink/salmon infill that clashes with the dark timber framing; across all builds the surface relief, window detail, lantern, and shuttered articulation of the concept are absent, keeping even the best candidates well below the target.

A and D use cream/off-white wall infill panels that match the concept's Tudor half-timber plaster aesthetic, while B, C, E, F, and G substitute pink/salmon tones — a material error that breaks the palette — and all seven candidates share the same structural shortfalls versus the concept: no stepped eave trim with contrast border, plain windows without shutters, no door lantern, and simplified timber-framing relief.
